violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: 1) in 2DR prep top, salad cooler: diced tomato (46F), black beans (65F)
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. CFM STATED THE ITEMS WERE PLACE IN THE PREP COOLER 1.5 HOURS PRIOR. CFM MOVED THE ITEMS TO A WORKING COOLER TO COOL THE FOOD QUICKLY TO 41F OR BELOW.

violations.title: RTE TCS Food, Disposition
violations.observation: Observed the following ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food being held for more than the specified time/temperature allowed: TUNA SALAD IN THE PREP COOLER WAS DATE MARKED SEPTEMBER 25.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be discarded if it: 1) exceeds 7 days or at 41F (except the time it is frozen); or 2) is in a container or package that does not bear a date or day. CFM DISCARDED THE TUNA SALAD.

out_items.name: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used

violations.title: Sanitizers, Criteria
violations.observation: The concentration of the QUATERNARY AMMONIUM solution in a sanitizer bucket was measured above 400ppm. The concentration exceeds the approved limits for use with food-contact surfaces of equipment and utensils in a foodservice establishment.
violations.corrective_action: Maintain the concentration of quaternary ammonium solution at 200-400ppm. Verify concentration using the appropriate test kit. The sanitizing solution was diluted during the inspection to the proper concentration.

out_items.name: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control

violations.title: Methods to Facilitate Cooling in Equipment
violations.observation: The following methods used for cooling were not adequate to facilitate proper cooling: COMMERCIALLY CANNED BLACK BEANS PLACED IN PREP COOLER TOP. PRODUCT WAS 65F DURING THE INSPECTION.
violations.corrective_action: Cooling hot foods shall be accomplished as follows: 1) placing the food in shallow pans; 2) separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; 3) using rapid cooling equipment; 4) stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; 5) using containers that facilitate heat transfer; 6) adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Food containers placed in cooling and cold equipment to cool shall be: 1) arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the containers walls, and 2) loosely covered or uncovered as long as protected from contamination to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food. EHS AND CFM DISCUSSED THE NEED TO COOL TCS FOOD IN EQUIPMENT CAPABLE OF QUICKLY LOWERING THE TEMPERATURE TO 41F OR BELOW. CFM MOVED AFOREMENTIONED FOODS TO A WORKING COOLER TO COOL TO 41F.

violations.title: Proper Thawing Methods for ROP Fish
violations.observation: OBSERVED THAWED SALMON FILLETS STILL IN THE MANUFACTURER VACUUM PACKAGING.
violations.corrective_action: SALMON FILLETS WERE REMOVED FROM THE REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING.

violations.title: RTE TCS Food Prepared On Site, Date Marking
violations.observation: The following refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food that is prepared on site is not used or discarded within 24 hours of preparation and was not observed to be date marked: 1) tomato sauce
violations.corrective_action: Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that are prepared on site and kept for more than 24 hours cannot have a shelf-life of more than 7 days, including the day of preparation. These food items must be marked with either the 'consume-by' date and/or 'preparation' date, color-coded labels, or another marking system/method that effectively indicates shelf-life that is clearly understood and properly used by the employees. PIC DISCARDED THE FOOD.

violations.observation: The following methods used for cooling were not adequate to facilitate proper cooling: 1) food is being prepped in the morning and being placed in the 2DR prep top salad cooler without cooling to 41f first

out_items.name: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible

violations.title: Handwashing Signage
violations.observation: The hand washing sinks at the server station, bar, and kitchen were observed without a hand washing sign.
violations.corrective_action: Provide a visible sign or poster at all handwashing sinks used by food employees that reminds food employees to wash their hands. POST A HAND WASHING SIGN AT THESE SINKS.

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal and RTE Foods
violations.observation: Observed Raw shelled eggs and Raw burger patties being stored over Ready-To-Eat food in the left 1DR glass cooler.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods like poultry, beef, pork, seafood, and eggs from cooked foods, ready-to- eat foods, washed produce, etc during storage, preparation, holding or display. Raw foods shall be stored on shelving units BELOW or SEPARATED from all cooked foods, commercially processed foods, washed produce, leftover foods, etc. PIC MOVED THE RAW FOOD TO THE BOTTOM OF THE COOLER.

out_items.name: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used

violations.title: Separation of Poison/Toxic Materials
violations.observation: Observed a disinfectant spray bottle being stored on the counter next to coffee products and ice.
violations.corrective_action: All poisonous and toxic materials shall be stored to prevent contamination of food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single service items by separating the poisonous and toxic materials by spacing or partitioning. PIC MOVE THE SPRAY BOTTLE AWAY TO A LOWER SHELF.

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: Observed the ice scoop lying in the ice.
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently. PIC STUCK THE ICE SCOOP INTO THE ICE WITH ITS HANDLE STICKING UPWARDS. HIDDEN CREEK CLUB BANQUET HALL (Inspection Date: 05/13/2025) Page 2 of 3

violations.title: Chemical Sanitization, Quaternary Ammonium Requirements
violations.observation: When tested, the quaternary ammonium compound-based sanitizing solution was observed to be at a concentration less than what is required for effective sanitization of food-contact surfaces of equipment and utensils. Hose was tightened onto supply mechanism - new solution registered at 150ppm.
